summary.title: 3D Computer Graphics Primer: Ray-Tracing as an Example
summary.one_liner: You learn how a 3D scene becomes a 2D image through perspective projection and shading, using ray-tracing as the introductory example.
keywords: light and color in computer graphics
takeaways: A 3D scene is turned into a 2D image in two steps: projecting object outlines onto an image plane, then shading the interior.
Perspective projection draws lines from object points to the eye and marks where they cross the image plane.
Object color comes from which light wavelengths a material absorbs versus reflects, and energy is conserved across absorption, reflection and transmission.
Materials are split into conductors (metals) and dielectrics (non-metals), which differ in how they interact with light.
The lesson is aimed at beginners and includes a short compilable ray-tracing program of a few hundred lines.
summary.summary: This Scratchapixel lesson introduces 3D computer graphics for beginners, using ray-tracing as the vehicle rather than a deep dive into the technique. It explains perspective projection onto an image plane, then covers how light, photons, materials (conductors and dielectrics) and color determine shading. It also gives historical context on theories of vision, including Ibn al-Haytham's. The lesson is meant to be paired with a small compilable ray-tracer program, and it points to other lessons for scanline rendering and deeper ray-tracing material.
